flagged.evidence: Clause 2 states: "For z,w in rho(A) the resolvent identity gives BR_A(z) = BR_A(w) + (z-w)BR_A(w)R_A(z)". With the library convention R_A(z) = (z-A)^{-1} the resolvent identity is R_A(z) - R_A(w) = (w-z)R_A(z)R_A(w), i.e. BR_A(z) = BR_A(w) - (z-w)BR_A(w)R_A(z); the displayed sign is wrong. Counterexample: A = 0 (self-adjoint) and B = I on C, z = 2, w = 3: the left side is 1/2, while the written right side is 1/3 + (2-3)(1/3)(1/2) = 1/6. The independence-of-z conclusion survives with the corrected sign, but the displayed identity is false.

[A2] states R_S(z) - 1/(lambda-z) I = -(1/(lambda-z)) R_S(z)(S-lambda) on D(S). Since R_S(z)(S-lambda) = -I + (z-lambda)R_S(z), the correct identity is R_S(z) + 1/(lambda-z) I = -(1/(lambda-z)) R_S(z)(S-lambda). Counterexample S = 0 on C, z = i, lambda = 1: left side = -i - 1/(1-i) = -1/2 - (3/2)i, right side = -(1/(1-i))(-i)(-1) = (1-i)/2, not equal. Step 1.1 then exports the same wrong sign as "(R_A(z) - 1/(lambda-z))x_n -> 0"; for a Weyl sequence one actually gets R_A(z)x_n -> (1/(z-lambda))x_n, so that difference tends to (2/(z-lambda))x_n, not 0. The transfer argument needs the plus sign; as written the input to step 2.1 is not licensed.

Property 2 first asserts C^{-1} = C^* = (T+i)(T-i)^{-1} and then says "one gets C^* = I - 2i(T-i)^{-1}". Since C = I - 2i(T+i)^{-1}, adjunction gives C^* = I - conj(2i)((T+i)^{-1})^* = I + 2i(T-i)^{-1} = (T+i)(T-i)^{-1}; the printed minus contradicts the item's own header and is false: for T = 0 on C one has C = C^* = -1, while I - 2i(T-i)^{-1} = 1 - 2i/(-i) = 3. The unitarity conclusion remains correct, but the displayed adjoint and the "direct substitution" built on it are false as written.

The statement asserts "<x, f(E)x> = int f dE_x". The library convention is <h(E)x,y> = int h dE_{x,y} with E_{x,y}(B) = <E(B)x,y> (thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral statement 1; lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm), so y = x gives <h(E)x,x> = int h dE_x and hence <x, f(E)x> = conj(int f dE_x) = int conj(f) dE_x. Counterexample: H = C, E({pt}) = I, f = i, x = 1: <x, f(E)x> = -i but int f dE_x = i. Step 1.1 derives the same wrong identity from <x, f_n(E)x> = int f_n dE_x.

Step 1.1 displays "<Pf,g> = -i(f(1)conj(g(1)) - f(0)conj(g(0))) - i int f conj(g') = -i int f conj(g') = <f,Pg>". Integration by parts gives int f' conj(g) = f(1)conj(g(1)) - f(0)conj(g(0)) - int f conj(g'), hence <Pf,g> = -i int f' conj(g) = -i(boundary term) + i int f conj(g'), while <f,Pg> = i int f conj(g'); the bulk term must carry +i. Counterexample f = g = e^{2 pi i x} (both in D(P)): <Pf,g> = 2 pi, while the written middle expression gives -2 pi. The symmetry conclusion is true, but the displayed computation is false.

[A3] claims the first factor [I + (z'-z)R_A(z)]^{-1}, "being I + (z-z')R_A(z')", has norm at most 1 + |z'-z|/|Im z|. Since that factor equals I + (z-z')R_A(z'), the valid bound is 1 + |z'-z|/|Im z'| (the bound stated for the second factor); the printed bound fails when |Im z| > |Im z'|. Counterexample A = 0 on C, z = 100i, z' = i: the factor is [1 + (-99i)/(100i)]^{-1} = 100, while 1 + |z'-z|/|Im z| = 1.99. The parameter-independence conclusion (step 1.2) is still true with the correct bound on both factors.

Step 3.2 asserts that f(t) = inf sigma(S_t), described as "the infimum of the affine functions t -> <(A+tB)x,x>/||x||^2 over x in D(A)\{0}", "is concave and finite on [0,1]". Concavity follows, but the stated reason does not yield finiteness: an infimum of finite affine functions can be -infinity (e.g. inf_n (n - n t) for t in (0,1]), and the preceding steps do not exclude inf sigma(S_t) = -infinity, since a self-adjoint operator may have a resolvent point with a positive spectral gap and spectrum unbounded below (multiplication by a function equal to x for x <= -1 and to 1 for x >= -1/2 has spectrum (-infinity,-1] union {1}, with 0 in the resolvent set). The subsequent argument (f(0) >= gamma > -lambda, the dichotomy inf sigma(S_t) >= -lambda + rho or <= -lambda - rho, continuity of f, and the "downward jump" contradiction) needs f finite; as written the stated lower bound is not licensed by the given text, even though the bound itself is the standard true statement.

Step 3.1 obtains conj(H) - i conj(g) = c 1 and then writes "that is g = iH - conj(ic)". Solving gives conj(g) = -i(conj(H) - c), hence g = iH + conj(ic) = iH - i conj(c); the printed expression instead satisfies conj(H) - i conj(g) = -c. Counterexample g = 1 (then h = 0, H = 0, c = -i, and conj(H) - i conj(g) = -i = c holds): the printed formula gives -conj(i(-i)) = -1, not 1. Since the constant is free and every later use needs only g = iH + const (so g' = iH' = ih and h = -ig'), no concluded claim is affected.

The Statement's parenthetical says "the form changes only by the constant (c-c')||x||^2", and step 2.1 displays q_{c'}[x] = c'||x||^2 + int (lambda-c')dE_x = c||x||^2 + int (lambda-c)dE_x + (c'-c)||x||^2 with "the forms differ by the constant (c'-c)||x||^2". Both first expressions equal int lambda dE_x, so the second equality double-counts the shift: with A = 0 on C, c = 0, c' = -1, x = 1 one gets q_{c'}[x] = 0 while the written right side is 0 + (0-(-1)) = 1. What actually changes by (c-c')||x||^2 is the summand ||(A-cI)^{1/2}x||^2, not q_A (which is c-independent). The c-independence and closedness conclusions are correct.

The closing sentence says "the unitaries are the phases of the unit circle and the extensions are the boundary conditions f(1) = mu f(0)". For the minimal operator the unitaries K_+ -> K_- are the scalars lambda with |lambda| = ||e^{-x}||/||e^{x}|| = 1/e (cex-the-minimal-derivative-is-symmetric-not-self-adjoint, steps 2.1 and 3.2), and it is the boundary parameters mu, |mu| = 1, that run over the phases. The remark's substantive content (one-parameter family, no extra choice beyond the Hilbert-basis input) is unaffected.

Step 1.4 begins "with the eigenvectors phi_1,...,phi_{n-1} of the first n-1 eigenvalues", but when the eigenvalues below Lambda are exhausted before n-1 one has E_{n-1} = Lambda by the statement's convention, so no such n-1 eigenvectors exist and the construction of F (and [A4]'s hypothesis "orthogonal to the eigenspaces of the first n-1 eigenvalues") is unavailable for those n. The case closes immediately by padding F with arbitrary orthonormal vectors after taking the span of the eigenvectors below Lambda; then every unit x in Q(A) cap F-perp has E_x vanishing on the finitely many eigenvalues below Lambda, whose complement in sigma(A) lies in [Lambda,infinity), so q_A[x] >= Lambda = E_n and the bound still follows. Nonfatal, but the step as written does not cover the case E_{n-1} = Lambda.

coverage_note: All 49 scoped carriers (47 items plus the two pages) were opened and read in full, each exactly once, and the dependencies needed to test the load-bearing claims were opened: def-spectrum-and-resolvent-of-a-bounded-operator (convention R(lambda,T) = (lambda-T)^{-1}), def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space (linear in the first slot), lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm (E_{x,y}(B) = <E(B)x,y>), thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral (<Phi_E(h)x,x> = int h dE_x), thm-support-and-uniqueness-of-the-spectral-measure, lem-neumann-series, thm-closed-graph-theorem. Every claim and computation was re-derived from the current files rather than trusted to the reader report; all eleven reader repairs were re-verified independently (nine check out; the fixes to def-relative-compactness clause 2, thm-weyl-essential-spectrum-invariance [A2], def-cayley-transform property 2 and ex-periodic step 1.1 left or introduced wrong signs, flagged above). Findings rest on explicit scalar or one-dimensional counterexamples reproducible in seconds against the library's own conventions. Limitations, honestly stated: the run is offline, so the item-cited external sources (Teschl, Williams, Schnaubelt, Buehler-Salamon) could not be re-fetched and nothing here relies on them; my thm-kato-rellich finding concerns the written justification of finiteness of f, not the truth of the bound. The reader's five lesser observations were re-verified: I concur that the range-criterion cross-reference in step 4.1 is loose but true, and I flag the three that are false as written plus the min-max padding gap, all nonfatal (the reader's assessment of them is otherwise confirmed). The two page carriers' prose was read in full and matches the current items, except that the examples-page sentence "whose generator is exactly P on D(P)" reads loosely against the formal generator convention (the item says the generator is iP); I judged that a page-level shorthand rather than a defect and did not flag it. No other defect was found.
